title: It is a classical guitar waltz.
description:
It is a classical guitar waltz. Gran Vals, composed in 1902 by the Spanish guitarist Francisco Tarrega. Nokia used a short phrase from early in the piece.

Two executives picked the phrase. Anssi Vanjoki found the piece and showed it to Lauri Kivinen. Yle describes them as Nokia's sales and marketing director and its communications director.

It first rang on the Nokia 2110. BGR says the phone listed it as Ringtone Type 7.

A guitarist from Turku recorded it. Yle reports that Timo Korhonen was paid a fee and given his own Nokia 2110, and later regretted not asking for more.

It was Grande Valse before it was Nokia tune. The Grande Valse name arrived in 1997 and Nokia tune in 1998, according to both Wikipedia and BGR.

A guitar waltz from 1902 became the sound of Nokia.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nokia_tune - read. Established the excerpt is from Gran Vals by Francisco Tarrega, the 1993 choice by Anssi Vanjoki and Lauri Kivinen, first use on the Nokia 2110 in 1994, the name Grande valse on the 6110 in December 1997 and the rename to Nokia tune in 1998.
- https://www.bgr.com/2290878/where-famous-nokia-tune-ringtone-comes-from-history/ - read in full. Independently established composition in 1902, the 1993 pick by Vanjoki and Kivinen, the Nokia 2110 in 1994 where it was listed as Ringtone Type 7, and the names Grande Valse (1997) and Nokia Tune (1998).
- https://yle.fi/a/74-20117758 - read in full (Finnish, Yle, 1 December 2024). Established that the story began in 1902 in Spain, that Vanjoki (sales and marketing director) showed the piece to Kivinen (communications director) in 1993, the 2110 in 1994, and that Turku guitarist Timo Korhonen made the recording, was paid a fee plus his own 2110 phone, and later regretted not asking for more.
- https://blogs.windows.com/devices/2009/01/21/history-of-nokia-part-3-grand-valse/ - read in full. Established Tarrega (1852 to 1909) from Spain and that the tune arrived on the Nokia 2110 in 1994.
